meta.title: Chennai property-tax payment (current year, residential, known bill number) grid-only evidence ledger
meta.disclaimer: Independent research, not official advice. Grid-only benchmark run: sources and claims only, no nodes, edges, roadblocks or journeys. Desk research, no counter visited. Limitations: the corporation's published method for assessing property tax refers to a percentage table 'given above' and to location-wise basic rates 'furnished in the annexure', and neither is present on the page, which ends with the literal placeholder 'TO BE UPDATED'; the Property Tax Calculator link on the corporation's live property-tax page points to a third-party staging host over plain HTTP on a non-standard port and did not connect on the access date; the Know your Status link on the same page returned HTTP 404; the payment, status and receipt routes are public but were read only, with no zone, division, bill or sub number entered and no payment begun. Do not submit personal data through this ledger.

scenarios.label: Chennai property-tax payment on a known bill number
scenarios.summary: An individual owner pays the current year's property tax on a residential property already on the municipal register with a known identifier, by the municipal payment route, online portal first and counter or bank route second. First-time assessment, name transfer or mutation, arrears disputes, rebate eligibility beyond what the payment route itself states, and commercial property are excluded.

sources.title: Property Tax Online Payment route - Greater Chennai Corporation
sources.notes: Jurisdiction: Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India. Agency naming as displayed on the access date: 'GREATER CHENNAI CORPORATION'. Direct current observation of a public official interface reachable without login; the route was read only and no payment was begun. Shows no visible last-updated date. claims.text: The corporation's property tax rules and procedure page states that payment can be made online at www.chennaicorporation.gov.in with 'Nil' transaction fee by using a credit card, debit card or net banking.
claims.notes: An explicit zero for the online channel, recorded as a stated value under protocol section 3. It fixes the charge for using the channel, not the tax itself.

claims.text: The corporation's property tax rules and procedure page lists the modes of paying property tax as through the tax collectors, through eleven named banks under a walk-in payment system, at e-seva common service centres run by Tamil Nadu Arasu Cable Television Corporation in taluk offices, zonal offices, divisional offices and headquarters, and online.
claims.notes: A usable rule about where the tax may be paid. The cheque or demand draft instruction this claim previously also carried is recorded atomically at claim_chennai_ptax_revenue_officer_is_payee.

claims.text: The corporation's online payment and receipt routes require a zone number, division code, bill number and sub number, and both tell the citizen to ensure the property tax bill number before making payment.
claims.notes: Matches this scenario's premise of a known property identifier.

claims.text: The corporation's assessment method page states that property tax in Chennai city limits is a half-yearly tax calculated as a percentage of annual rental value, which is arrived at from the reasonable letting value under section 100 of the Chennai City Municipal Corporation Act 1919.
claims.notes: A half-yearly cycle, without any date on which a half year's tax falls due.

claims.text: The corporation's assessment method page states that the annual value of a building is obtained by multiplying the monthly rental value by the common factor 10.92, and works the derivation through a numeric example.
claims.notes: One half of the calculation is published; the rate to apply to the annual value is not.

claims.text: The corporation's assessment method page refers the citizen to a percentage table 'given above' for the half-yearly tax and to an annexure for location-wise basic rates per square foot, and neither the table nor the annexure appears anywhere on the page, which ends with the text 'TO BE UPDATED'.
claims.notes: Direct current observation of the page's own contents. The two missing pieces are exactly the two numbers a citizen needs to compute the tax.

claims.text: The corporation's assessment method page states that a 10 per cent library cess is calculated from the general tax component of property tax, citing G.O.Ms.No.492 dated 19 May 1992 and Council Resolution No.246/2001 dated 22 May 2001.
claims.notes: A rate that is published, applied to a base that is not.

claims.text: The corporation publishes a Property Tax Online Payment Receipt route, reachable without login, which returns a payment receipt for a property identified by its zone number, division code, bill number and sub number.
claims.notes: The observation is the route, its title and its four input fields on the access date; the inference is what it returns for a real property, since no identifier was entered and no case data was retrieved.

claims.text: The corporation publishes a Property Tax Status route and a Property Tax Payment Status route alongside the payment route, all reachable without login.
claims.notes: The routes were observed as published links and entry forms; neither was exercised.

claims.text: The corporation's payment and receipt routes both carry a note directing a citizen with any discrepancy in their property tax to submit complaints with particulars to the Revenue Officer, giving telephone numbers 2538 3614 and 2538 4510 extension 370.
claims.notes: A named role with a direct contact route, published on the payment surface itself. Institutional contact details only.

claims.text: The corporation's property tax rules and procedure page names 'The Revenue Officer, Corporation of Chennai' as the payee in whose favour a cheque or demand draft for property tax must be drawn.
claims.notes: The same role the discrepancy note points to, identified from a second route.

claims.text: The Property Tax Calculator link on the corporation's live property tax section index points to a third-party staging host, coc-staging.egovernments.org, over plain HTTP on port 9980, and the address did not connect on the access date.
claims.notes: Recorded as observed. The calculator is the route that would supply the missing rate, so its failure and the missing table are the same gap seen twice.

claims.text: The Know your Status link on the corporation's property tax section index returned HTTP 404 on the access date.

The document list the corporation publishes on its property tax rules and procedure page, comprising registered documents in the applicant's favour, a filled application Form-6 and the last tax paid receipt, is given for the submission of an application for assessment of property tax, not for paying tax on an existing assessment.
claims.notes: Recorded to mark the boundary with this scenario's excluded first-assessment route, not to support the documents cell.

claims.text: The date on which a half year's property tax falls due, and whether any penalty or rebate attaches to paying late or early, is not established by any reviewed public page.
claims.notes: Retained because the uncertainty itself matters to the journey. Not login-related; the payment route is public.

claims.text: The amount of property tax payable on a residential property for the current half year cannot be derived from any reviewed public page, because the percentage of annual value and the location-wise basic rate the corporation's own method depends on are both missing from the page that cites them.
claims.notes: Retained because the uncertainty itself matters to the journey. Not login-related; the calculator that would answer it points at an unreachable staging host.
